compilation.method: source-grounded structured model compilation with deterministic evidence and coverage validation
compilation.source: Final applicability criteria and exact source evidence in the frozen Module A records; prior pilot decisions were not used as a decision oracle.
compilation.scope: Seven reviewed rules only; not a universal natural-language compiler or complete legal calculation engine.
fact_binding_notes: Only jurisdiction, verified residential use/type and the explicit residential-rental query context are available to establish the general conditional protections.
A source-reported Units1 value is not building count, owner portfolio count, offered-for-rent count or a count at a different legal geography.
Owner portfolio facts require owner identity, geographic scope, property/unit definitions and observation date; property_unit facts require the evaluated unit/building identity.
All transaction, tenancy, household and legal-context facts are unknown unless separately supplied with the expected subject scope and provenance.
Elapsed-time, ratio and excess arithmetic inputs must identify their original operands and event dates. These specialized inputs are not automatically derived by this pilot binder.

branches.label: Abandoned-property content in inspection notice

exclusions.reason: A defined screening fee is not security; this affects only the subject payment.

unknown.reason: The substantive CCP 1161(2)-(4) grounds are not supplied; a reported statutory classification alone does not resolve that missing definition.

exclusions.reason: Subdivision (f) excludes the specified termination grounds, subject to their missing substantive definitions.
Informed no-request choice or prior withdrawal discharges subsequent inspection duties.

branches.duty: Include substantially the statutory abandoned-property statement in the written inspection notice.
retained_conditions: Use the exact underlying statutory statement: reclaiming abandoned property is conditional, storage and elapsed time may create costs, and prompt contact generally lowers costs.
A waiver signed by both parties concerns the 48-hour notice only. It does not waive all security protections or excuse defective content in a notice actually provided.
Tenant absence alone is not withdrawal.

Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Written notice under f(1) in applicable inspection procedure.

notes: Jurisdiction and current status are evaluated independently by the runtime.
plans.compilation_scope: Applicability and event triggers; compliance and amounts retained, not computed.

criteria_ledger.reason: Residential dwelling agreement and security payment functions are conjunctive scope requirements.
The complete defined screening transaction excludes only that payment from security.
Specified statutory grounds with source uncertainty embedded inside the exemption.
Informed no-request choice or prior withdrawal discharges subsequent duties; absence does not.
Requested procedure and provision of written notice trigger the retained content requirement.

fact_definitions.description: Landlord provided the subdivision (f)(1) written inspection notice.
Tenant was informed of the initial-inspection option before choosing.

Renewal-refusal alternative requires a written lease that terminated on or after 2023-06-24 AND landlord's written request or demand received by tenant AND tenant refusal to execute a written extension or renewal AND substantially similar duration AND substantially similar provisions AND lawful proposed terms.

Criminal-activity alternative requires tenant criminal activity on the property or associated common areas. Criminal-threat alternative requires a Penal Code 422(a) threat by tenant directed at landlord or another tenant of the property, wherever made.

Other alternatives: assignment OR sublet contrary to the lease under CCP 1161(4); OR refusal of entry authorized by Civil Code 1101.5 or 1954 and Health and Safety Code 13113.7 or 17926.1; OR unlawful use under CCP 1161(4).
Employment/agency/license alternative requires tenant status as landlord's employee, agent or licensee AND termination of that status AND failure to vacate, subject to CCP 1161(1).

Surrender alternative requires failure to deliver possession at the specified time AND either tenant's written termination notice under Civil Code 1946 OR tenant's written surrender offer accepted in writing by landlord, subject to CCP 1161(5).

For a curable lease violation, first give written notice describing the violation and an opportunity to cure under CCP 1161(3). Only if uncured within that notice's period may landlord serve a three-day quit notice without another cure opportunity.

branches.duty: Use a qualifying demolition or substantial-remodel ground and provide all required termination-notice information and documents.
retained_conditions: Ground requires intent to demolish OR substantial remodeling. Substantial remodeling requires (((replacement OR substantial modification of a structural, electrical, plumbing, or mechanical system) AND governmental permit required) OR lawful hazardous-material abatement) AND work that cannot reasonably be safely accomplished while the tenant remains AND at least 30 consecutive days of required vacancy.

Cosmetic improvements alone, including painting, decorating, and minor repairs, and work safely performed while occupied do not qualify. Tenants need not vacate on days they may safely and lawfully remain under health, safety, and habitability laws.

Written notice must state demolition/remodel intent AND provide the applicable work description and approximate remodel duration OR expected demolition date AND attach required permit copies OR, only for hazardous-material abatement requiring no permit, a signed contractor agreement reasonably detailing the abatement work.

Notice must include the prescribed conditional return-right statement and both 30-day clocks, and instruct a tenant interested in returning after remodeling to communicate interest and provide address, telephone number, and email address.

Notice/ground defects are potential violations, not coverage exclusions. No unconditional right to return after successfully completed work or independent work commencement/completion deadline is supplied.
Section operative April 1, 2024; supplied version effective January 1, 2026; repeal January 1, 2030.

branches.duty: Do not terminate a covered tenancy without a qualifying at-fault OR no-fault cause stated in the written termination notice.
retained_conditions: Cause validity and a written statement are compliance requirements; an attempted termination without either remains covered.

At-fault alternatives: rent-payment default; material lease breach under Section 1161(3), including a violation after written corrective notice; statutory nuisance; statutory waste; qualifying renewal refusal; specified criminal activity/threat; prohibited assignment/subletting; refusal of legally authorized entry; statutory unlawful use; failure to vacate after employee/agent/licensee termination; or failure to surrender under the specified tenant notice/accepted written offer.

Renewal refusal requires a written lease that ended on/after January 1, 2020, or January 1, 2022 for a mobilehome AND the owner's written request/demand AND tenant refusal to execute a written extension/renewal of similar duration and similar provisions AND proposed terms lawful under this section and other law.

Criminal ground requires tenant criminal activity on the residential property, including common areas, OR criminal activity or a Penal Code 422(a) criminal threat on or off the property directed at an owner or owner's agent.

Assignment/subletting must violate the lease and satisfy incorporated Section 1161(4). Entry refusal must concern entry authorized by Civil Code 1101.5 or 1954 or Health and Safety Code 13113.7 or 17926.1.

Nonsurrender requires failure to deliver possession at the specified time after the tenant's written termination notice under Section 1946 OR the tenant's written surrender offer accepted in writing by the owner, subject to Section 1161(5). Ended employee/agent/licensee occupancy is subject to Section 1161(1).

No-fault alternatives: qualifying owner/family primary-residence occupancy OR withdrawal from the rental market OR compliance with a government/court habitability order necessitating vacancy, a government/court order to vacate, or a local ordinance necessitating vacancy OR qualifying demolition/substantial remodeling.

Owner-occupancy ground requires intent for the owner, spouse, domestic partner, child, grandchild, parent, or grandparent to occupy as primary residence for at least 12 continuous months. For leases entered on/after July 1, 2020, or July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes, require tenant written agreement to termination OR a lease provision permitting the specified unilateral owner/family move-in termination. Adding such a provision to a new/renewed agreement is a similar provision for renewal-refusal purposes.

Owner-occupancy ground fails if the intended occupant already occupies a rental unit on the property OR a similar unit is already vacant. Notice must identify intended occupants and relationships and advise of the right to request ownership/relationship proof; supply proof upon request, including nonpublic documents if necessary.

Owner-occupancy timing requires move-in within 90 days after vacancy AND at least 12 consecutive months as primary residence. Failure requires an offer to the displaced tenant at rent and terms at vacancy AND reimbursement of reasonable moving expenses exceeding relocation assistance already paid. Timely move-in followed by death before 12 months is not the specified failure or material violation. New letting during clause (v)'s periods uses lawful rent at termination-notice service.

Owner for this ground includes a natural person with at least 25 percent recorded ownership OR a natural person with any recorded interest where all recorded ownership is divided among owners related as sibling, spouse, domestic partner, child, parent, grandparent, or grandchild OR a natural person whose recorded interest is owned through an LLC or partnership.

Natural person includes a settlor or beneficiary of a family trust and, for LLC/partnership ownership, a beneficial owner with at least 25 percent property ownership. Family trust means revocable living or irrevocable trust whose settlors and beneficiaries have the specified family relationships. Beneficial owner means a natural person or family trust exercising substantial LLC/partnership control OR owning at least 25 percent entity equity OR receiving substantial economic benefits from partnership assets, directly or indirectly through the described arrangements.

For government/court/local-law vacancy, a government or court determination that the tenant caused the triggering conditions removes the specified relocation assistance; it does not remove just-cause protection.

Substantial remodel requires (((replacement OR substantial modification of structural, electrical, plumbing, or mechanical systems) AND permit required) OR lawful hazardous-material abatement) AND work cannot reasonably be safely done while tenant remains AND at least 30 consecutive days of required vacancy. Cosmetic work alone and safely occupied work do not qualify; tenant need not leave on lawful and safe occupancy days. Demolition is a separate intent alternative.

Demolition/remodel notice must state intent; give remodel description and expected duration OR demolition date; attach required permits OR, only for permitless hazardous abatement, a signed detailed contractor agreement; include the prescribed conditional return statement and tenant-interest/contact instructions. Work not commenced OR not completed requires rerental on prior terms and vacancy rent, with 30 days after receipt to respond and 30 days after acceptance notification to reoccupy.
Section operative April 1, 2024; supplied version effective January 1, 2026; repeal January 1, 2030. Lease-end and exemption-notice cutoffs do not establish when every current amendment detail began.

branches.label: Dominant-motive just cause

source_gates.reason: Full statutory prerequisites for incorporated grounds, especially owner-relative occupancy, are not supplied. They affect whether an eviction complies, not whether just cause is required.

branches.duty: Have a qualifying just-cause reason as the dominant motive for pursuing eviction.
retained_conditions: Just cause must be the landlord's dominant motive. Mere agreement expiration OR ownership change is insufficient; a landlord lacking just cause still owes this duty.
The 17 summarized grounds are alternatives, each subject to its internal conditions and any missing statutory prerequisites.
1. Nonpayment OR habitual late payment OR frequent bounced checks.
2. Substantial lease/agreement breach AND failure to cure.
3. Nuisance OR substantial interference with landlord/other tenants' comfort, safety or enjoyment, with severity OR continuing OR recurring nature.
4. Illegal use, excluding mere occupancy of an unwarranted unit OR a single Chapter 41A violation cured within 30 days of the landlord's written notice.
5. Expired agreement AND landlord written renewal/extension request AND like duration AND materially identical terms AND tenant refusal.
6. Legally required landlord access AND written notice to cease refusal AND tenant refusal to allow access.
7. At agreement term end the sole remaining occupant is a subtenant AND lacks landlord approval. Approval can be written OR oral OR implied by conduct.
8. Owner occupancy OR immediate-family occupancy in limited circumstances whose full conditions are absent.
9. Good-faith recovery to sell the unit AND condominium conversion approved under the SF subdivision ordinance.
10. Demolition OR permanent removal of an individual rental unit from housing use.
11. Capital improvements OR rehabilitation causing temporary uninhabitability during work; tenant must be allowed immediate reoccupancy after completion.
12. Substantial rehabilitation AND building at least 50 years old AND essentially uninhabitable AND proposed work cost at least 75% of new-construction cost.
13. Ellis Act withdrawal of ALL rental units in the building.
14. Lead remediation/abatement required by SF Health Code Articles 11 OR 26.
15. Demolition OR permanent removal from housing use in accordance with a City development agreement under Administrative Code Chapter 56.

16. Expired Good Samaritan occupancy agreement AND eviction notice served within 60 days after expiry. Good Samaritan occupancy requires emergency OR disaster displacement AND temporary replacement housing AND reduced rent provided by agreement.
17. Development project requiring demolition of the existing property under Planning Code Section 317.
The 30-day cure, 60-day post-expiry notice and building-age tests are retained compliance tests, not query-date substitutes or coverage/event predicates.

notes: Ground sufficiency and dominant motive are compliance requirements. Encoding them as event prerequisites would incorrectly exclude unlawful evictions from this protection. Rent-control exclusions do not automatically exclude eviction coverage.

Building rental-unit count and prior use are explicit static eligibility tests; clause 3's owner holdings/home counting meaning is an unresolved source subtree, not an invented ownership or count predicate. The intended-relative restriction and qualified-household amount remain separate branches.
The manager-only conflict is gated by its own asserted event; the missing complete section 151.30 is independently preserved at calculation stage.

The annual amounts appear as source-grounded candidate modifiers, but the unconditional unresolved calculation gate prevents resolved_effects from returning them. There is no implemented net-offset, highest-entitlement or pro-rata arithmetic.

A verified building count above four defeats this narrow reduction without requiring unrelated owner facts. This is out of scope for the permission, not a statutory exemption from ordinary relocation assistance.

D043 clause 3 says no more than four residential units and a single-family home on a separate Los Angeles lot. Without full LAMC 151.30, the pilot does not resolve whether the home is an allowed additional holding, whether one must be owned, or how that home enters the unit-count ceiling.

branches.duty: Apply the four alternative removal grounds and their notice and relocation safeguards.
retained_conditions: Serve Notice to Quit at least three months before filing. Provide required relocation assistance before eviction.
G(3) illegal-occupancy removal entitles tenant to six times monthly rent, payable by landlord at least five days before removal.
If payment is not received timely, tenant may receive payment from an established municipal revolving fund; landlord must repay the municipality.
If no municipal fund exists AND landlord fails to pay timely, unpaid balance accrues 18% annual interest until principal and interest are paid in full; amount due is a lien on the property.
